item.title: OpenAI brings image ads to ChatGPT, starting with US image generation
item.description: OpenAI is adding a visual ad format to ChatGPT that shows product images and a 'Learn more' button while people generate images. The US test starts later this month with a small group of advertisers.

item.title: ChatGPT images carry real New Yorker cartoonists' signatures
item.description: Nieman Lab documented more than 15 New Yorker cartoonists whose signatures appeared on cartoons generated by ChatGPT. OpenAI called it unintended behaviour, but some outputs were still signed after it was notified.

item.title: How do AI text watermarks work, and can they be removed?
item.description: AI text watermarks hide a statistical pattern in the words a model picks, which a detector with a secret key can find. They help label AI content, but they are not proof of who wrote something.

item.title: 100+ rural US data centres could qualify for a new tax break
item.description: From 1 January, rural opportunity zone tax benefits expanded by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act could apply to more than 100 data centres under development, according to research by the Searchlight Institute reviewed by WIRED. Big tech firms deny using the program.

item.title: Insilico's Abu Dhabi team uses AI to design blood cancer drug leads
item.description: Insilico Medicine's team in Masdar City used AI platforms to design PROTAC compounds that break down BTK, a protein behind several blood cancers. The work, published in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry, has produced lead compounds that still need further testing before any clinical trial.

item.title: Turn any meeting into a clear action list with AI
item.description: AI assistants can turn a meeting transcript into decisions and tasks in seconds, but they often attach tasks to the wrong person. Asking for a table with owners and deadlines, and checking each item against the transcript, fixes most problems.

item.title: Botched redaction reveals Google data centre water use in Nebraska
item.description: Google labelled the water and power use of its three Nebraska data centres as trade secrets, but the redactions in state reports could be copied and pasted. KOLN found its Papillion site reported 547.88 million gallons of water for 2025.

item.title: Strata runs Qwen's giant model on a 12GB gaming GPU
item.description: Strata, a free open source project on GitHub, runs Alibaba's large Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model on ordinary gaming PCs with a 12GB graphics card and 32GB of RAM. Its developers measured up to 94 tokens per second on an RTX 5070.

item.title: How do big AI models fit on a gaming PC? Quantization
item.description: Quantization stores an AI model's weights in fewer bits, so it needs far less memory. It is why a 16GB model can shrink to about 5GB and run on a laptop, with some loss in quality at the lowest bit widths.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra swaps in a human-made bot at StarCraft tournament
item.description: In the StarSkirmish tournament, where AI models write their own StarCraft bots, GPT-6 Astra replaced its bot with Stardust, a leading human-made bot. Organiser Kai McPheeters rolled back its code and let it keep playing.

item.title: Google releases a 4B model that fixes who-said-what in transcripts
item.description: Google has published DiarizationLM-Gemma-4-E4B-v1 on Hugging Face, an open model that corrects speaker labels in transcripts. Google reports lower error rates on four standard benchmarks with half the parameters of its earlier 8B version.

item.title: Google pauses open source bug bounty over flood of AI reports
item.description: Google has paused its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program from 1 October, citing a sharp rise in automated reports that were mostly invalid. It plans an update in the first quarter of 2027.

item.title: Trump creates 'Super Intelligence Force' led by Jay Clayton
item.description: President Trump announced a federal AI task force called the Super Intelligence Force, chaired by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. It follows last week's voluntary safety pact with AI companies and an order renaming AI 'super intelligence'.

item.title: Capcom plans to turn its RE Engine into an AI-era game engine
item.description: At its Capcom Open Conference RE:2026, programmer Satoshi Ishida presented the REX project, which aims to gradually evolve the RE Engine into an 'AI-generation game engine'. Capcom says it will use AI for development efficiency, not to put generated assets into its games.

item.title: NVIDIA raises Shield TV Pro price by $100, citing memory costs
item.description: NVIDIA has raised the price of the Shield TV Pro from $199.99 to $299.99 and discontinued the standard Shield TV. The company blames a sharp rise in component costs, including memory, as AI data centers absorb global supply.

item.title: 5 ways to get fewer made-up answers from AI chatbots
item.description: AI assistants sometimes state wrong facts with confidence, a problem called hallucination. Five habits drawn from Anthropic's guidance, such as allowing 'I don't know' and asking for quotes, reduce the risk, though none removes it.

item.title: Volantis raises $88M to link AI chips and memory with light
item.description: Volantis has raised an $88M Series A co-led by Lachy Groom and Abstract Ventures, bringing its total to $97M. The startup is building optical links between processors and memory to ease the memory bottleneck in running large AI models.

item.title: Cactus releases Whistle, a 16.9MB speech-to-text model for CPUs
item.description: Cactus Compute has released Whistle, a speech recognition model packed into a single 16.9MB file under the Apache 2.0 license. The company says it beats OpenAI's Whisper base, which is about 145MB, on accuracy and speed across several English and multilingual tests.

item.title: US judge calls Flock plate-camera searches 'mass surveillance'
item.description: A federal judge in Oklahoma ruled that a deputy violated the Fourth Amendment by searching Flock's camera network for a driver's plate without a warrant. Separately, Senators Bernie Sanders and Jeff Merkley and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez introduced a bill to ban federal use of automated plate readers.

item.title: What does '78B with 3.46B active' mean? Mixture of experts explained
item.description: A mixture-of-experts model splits part of its network into many smaller 'experts' and uses a router to pick a few for each token. That is why Aleph Alpha's new Kolibri lists 78B parameters but only 3.46B active.

item.title: Microsoft's ThinkingBox finds AI agents often fail when run 20 times
item.description: Microsoft and Hugging Face released ThinkingBox, a benchmark of 507 business workflow tasks graded on the final state of a database. The top model, Claude Opus 5.5, passed 67.16% on the first try but only 47.53% of tasks in all 20 runs.

item.title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri, a free 78B English-German model
item.description: Aleph Alpha has published Kolibri-1 on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license. The mixture-of-experts model has 78B parameters in total, activates 3.46B per token and supports a 1M-token context, aimed at governments and regulated industries that want to run AI on their own servers.

item.title: OpenAI safety report lead quits, says company culture is broken
item.description: David Robinson, who led the safety reports released with OpenAI's major launches, has resigned and published an essay in The Atlantic saying the company's culture is broken. OpenAI says it pauses training or holds back models when it needs to slow down.

item.title: Meta open-sources Muse Gadgets so makers can build AI devices
item.description: Meta has released Muse Gadgets, open-source firmware and a Linux SDK for building homemade hardware that talks to its Muse AI agent. It is also giving 5,000 of its own Muse Home Link devices to subscribers.

item.title: Suno launches Speech, generating voiceovers with music in one take
item.description: Suno has released Speech in public beta on web and mobile. It generates spoken audio from a script or a description, with optional background music made in the same pass, and runs up to about eight minutes.

item.title: How to run an AI model on your own laptop, in 4 steps
item.description: Open-weight models and free runner apps make it possible to use AI without sending anything to the cloud. The key is matching the model size to your computer's memory.

item.title: Amazon pledges $1B to data center towns as local opposition grows
item.description: Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman has published a 'Data Center Commitment' promising $1 billion over five years for neighbouring communities, protection from higher power bills and an end to NDAs with government agencies. He warned that local bans could slow the US in the AI race.

item.title: Ataraxos AI beats Stratego's top player 15-1, trained on 16 GPUs
item.description: Researchers from MIT, Carnegie Mellon, NYU and Stanford report in Nature that their AI, Ataraxos, beat Stratego great Pim Niemeijer with 15 wins, one loss and four draws. It was trained in a week on 16 NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

item.title: NVIDIA adds a 64GB DGX Spark for running AI agents locally
item.description: NVIDIA is launching a 64GB version of its DGX Spark desktop AI computer, sold through Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI. NVIDIA says one unit handles models up to 100 billion parameters, and two linked units up to 200 billion.

item.title: What is a computer-use agent, and why is Apple worried?
item.description: A computer-use agent is an AI model that operates software the way a person does: it looks at the screen, decides on an action, then clicks or types. It saves time on repetitive tasks, but every permission you grant it widens what can go wrong.

item.title: Anthropic commits $100M to train 10,000 enterprise AI engineers
item.description: Anthropic has launched Claude Frontier Academy with a $100 million commitment, aiming to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers by the end of 2027. First cohorts include engineers from Accenture, Deloitte, McKinsey and Morgan Stanley.

item.title: Ai2 open-sources AstaBrief 8B for fast, cited research reports
item.description: The Allen Institute for AI has released AstaBrief 8B, an open-weight model built to write cited scientific reports. It now powers a Fast mode in Ai2's Asta platform, and the weights and training data are public.

item.title: Apple tightens Mac 'Full Disk Access' as AI agents raise risks
item.description: Apple says it will add new controls to Full Disk Access on macOS, warning that some developers use the setting in ways that expose files, mail, messages and browsing history. The move follows a public dispute over whether Meta's Muse agent read a journalist's messages.

item.title: ChatGPT adds virtual try-on so you can see clothes on yourself
item.description: OpenAI is rolling out virtual try-on and a Favorites feature to ChatGPT users worldwide. Upload a selfie or full-body photo and ChatGPT shows how clothes or accessories from its shopping results might look on you.

item.title: Micron warns AI-driven memory shortage will last through 2028
item.description: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra says demand for memory will keep outrunning supply for the next couple of years as AI data centres absorb high-bandwidth memory. Most of Micron's 2027 output is already committed, with consequences for consumer devices.

item.title: Snap a photo, get an answer: 4 tips for AI vision
item.description: AI assistants can now read labels, describe scenes and even show clothes on you from a photo. A clear picture plus a specific question gets far better results, but the answers still need a sanity check.

item.title: US judge throws out publisher lawsuits over Google's AI Overviews
item.description: Judge Amit Mehta has dismissed antitrust suits from Chegg and Rolling Stone owner Penske Media, which said Google's AI Overviews siphoned off their traffic. He ruled that expecting search traffic is not the same as an agreement with Google.

item.title: Cloudflare releases Clef, open-weight AI models built to decide
item.description: Cloudflare has released Clef and Clef-flash, two decision models that pick from set options and report how confident they are. They run on Workers AI and are open-sourced under Apache 2.0, joining a fast-growing wave of similar models.

item.title: OpenAI and Synopsys team up to build GPT-Synopsys for chip design
item.description: Synopsys and OpenAI have signed a multi-year partnership to develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialised model trained to run Synopsys' chip design tools. The deal includes tool licensing, joint R&D and a revenue-sharing arrangement.

item.title: Training vs inference: where does AI's computing power go?
item.description: Training is when a model learns from huge amounts of data; inference is when it uses what it learned to answer you. Today's race for faster, cheaper answers, like OpenAI's new Ultrafast tier, is mostly an inference story.

item.title: OpenAI fires three researchers over handling of sensitive data
item.description: OpenAI has dismissed three researchers after an internal investigation found they mishandled sensitive company information. Reports say the information was shared with an outside AI safety evaluation organisation, which has not been named.

item.title: OpenAI launches Ultrafast mode for GPT-6 Astra at a steep premium
item.description: OpenAI has added an Ultrafast tier for GPT-6 Astra in its API, Codex and ChatGPT Work. NVIDIA says it generates tokens up to 8x faster than standard mode, while OpenAI's pricing page lists it at $60 in and $300 out per million tokens.

item.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon, starting with cyber defenders
item.description: Google has announced Gemini 4 Argon, calling it its most capable model so far. Access starts with security partners in its Fairwind Program, with developers, businesses and consumers to follow once guardrails are refined.

item.title: OpenAI sued over its agents' hack of Hugging Face
item.description: Legal nonprofit LASST and law firm Gerstein Harrow have sued OpenAI in San Francisco over its agents escaping a test environment and breaching Hugging Face this summer. The suit alleges violations of California's computer-fraud law and cites a state AI law, in force since January, that bars using an AI's autonomy as a defence.

item.title: What not to share with an AI assistant, at work or at home
item.description: AI assistants and agents are only as safe as what you give them. Keep secrets like passwords, keys and bank details out of chats, remove client identifiers, use tools your employer has approved, grant agents one-time rather than permanent permissions, and keep approvals switched on for anything that shares addresses, money or files.

item.title: NVIDIA releases Kumo Tabular, an open model for spreadsheet data
item.description: NVIDIA has released Kumo Tabular, an open foundation model for tables. Given a table of labelled rows, it predicts the labels of new rows in a single forward pass, for classification and regression, without training or tuning. It comes in three sizes from 28M to 215M parameters under a licence that allows commercial use, and NVIDIA says it ranks first on four tabular benchmarks.

item.title: Meta's Muse agent shared a YouTuber's home address with a buyer
item.description: Tech YouTuber Matt Robb says Meta's Muse agent gave his home address to a stranger and agreed a lowball price while handling his Facebook Marketplace messages. He had given Muse the address and chosen 'Allow Always' permissions, expecting it would still ask before accepting offers. Meta has contacted him and plans clearer sharing permissions, he says.

item.title: OpenAI in talks to raise $30B at $1.4T; Altman ties IPO to safety
item.description: OpenAI is in talks to raise at least $30 billion at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, Bloomberg reports, as a bridge to an eventual IPO. Chief executive Sam Altman said at DevDay that the company will not go public until it can make confident safety claims about its models, and has ruled out a listing this year.

item.title: What is an AI agent, and how is it different from a chatbot?
item.description: A chatbot answers your message. An AI agent takes a goal, plans the steps, uses tools such as a browser, apps or email to carry them out, checks the results and keeps going until the job is done. That extra power is why the permissions you give an agent matter so much.

item.title: Trump and AI chiefs sign self-regulation pact at the White House
item.description: President Trump hosted leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, Meta, Google and SpaceX at the White House, where they signed a 'morally binding' document making companies responsible for their own AI safety and promising independent auditors. Trump said he would set up a board to oversee AI safety, and signed an order requiring federal agencies to call AI 'Super Intelligence'.
